transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope it's okay that I'm here. It's probably nothing major, just... well, I work as a video editor and camera operator, and I guess what finally scared me into coming in is that I keep making these... kind of silly technical mistakes? 

I mean, I know better than to make them, I really do. But I'll catch myself doing things like labeling camera cards wrong, or missing a timecode note. I even exported a client cut recently with the wrong lower-third, and the embarrassing part is I swear I checked it before I sent it out. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job and not messing up my team's workflow, you know? Does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you might be able to help me with?
Have you noticed any difficulties with concentration, memory, or attention in other areas of your life, not just at work?

Um... not really? I mean, I don't think so. I try really hard to keep everything together at home, so... I don't want to make it sound like my whole life is a mess, because it's really not! 

I mean, maybe I'll forget to grab something at the grocery store every now and then, or misplace my keys for a second, but that's just normal, right? Everyone does that. I'm usually pretty on top of things outside of the edit bay. I hope I'm answering that right... I just haven't really noticed anything too bad outside of those silly work mistakes I mentioned. Is that okay?
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy lately?

Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I don't think I've been feeling down or anything like that. I actually really love my job, and I have a good life. I try to stay positive, you know? 

I guess I get a little frustrated with myself when I make those mistakes at work, but I definitely wouldn't say I feel hopeless. I still really enjoy editing and working on projects. I just want to fix this little hiccup so I can get back to doing my best. I hope that's the right answer... I'm not depressed or anything, I promise. I just want to be better at my job. Is that what you meant?
Do you often find yourself struggling to stay organized or keep track of tasks, even when you're not at work?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I try to keep everything at home pretty tidy. I have a planner, and I try to write things down so I don't forget them. 

I guess sometimes my desk gets a little messy, or I'll start organizing a closet and then get distracted by something else and leave it half done... but I always go back and finish it eventually! I really try my best to keep on top of things. I don't want you to think I'm just this chaotic person who can't manage her life, because I really do try hard. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Do you ever feel really anxious or worried about making mistakes, even small ones, or feel like others might be judging you for them?

Um... no, I wouldn't really say that. I mean, nobody really *likes* messing up, right? So if I make a little mistake on a cut or something, I might feel a tiny bit embarrassed for a second, but I just fix it and move on. 

I definitely don't sit around worrying that people are secretly judging me or anything like that. My team is really great, actually, and I try to just keep a good attitude about everything. I really don't want to sound like I'm super stressed out or, you know, paranoid, because I'm really not! I just try to do my best and be easy to work with. Is that... does that answer what you were asking?
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels lately, even if they don’t seem related to work stress?

Oh, um, no, everything's been pretty normal in that department. I make sure to eat pretty well, so my appetite is totally fine. And my sleep is good too! I mean, I try really hard to get to bed at a decent hour so I'm fresh for the editing bay the next morning. 

And my energy levels are great—I actually have a lot of energy, which I think is a good thing for my job, right? I wouldn't say there have been any weird changes or drops in energy or anything like that. I feel pretty healthy overall. 

Is it okay that nothing has really changed with all of that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and being helpful.
Have you ever experienced any strange or unusual thoughts, like hearing voices or seeing things that others don't, even if just briefly?

Oh, gosh, no. Nothing like that at all. I mean, I have a pretty active imagination because of my work with video and film, but I definitely don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. 

I feel like my mind is really grounded in reality, you know? I would never want you to think I'm losing touch with things or anything scary like that. Everything is completely normal in that way. I'm just a regular person who maybe has a little too much energy sometimes. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for.
Do you ever find yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or having trouble sitting still for long periods, even when you need to focus on something important?

Um, well, I guess I do move around a little bit, but it's really not a big deal! I mean, when we're in edit reviews, sometimes I'll, you know, click my pen a little, or maybe bounce my knee under the table... just small things to keep the blood flowing, right? 

Sometimes I roll my chair back and forth a tiny bit, but it's just because I'm really engaged with the work! Actually, my coworkers have started joking that they can hear me before they see me, which is kind of funny, I think. It's just a little quirk, you know? It doesn't mean I'm not paying attention or anything. I'm still totally focused on the edits! 

I hope that doesn't make me sound unprofessional or anything. I just have a lot of enthusiasm for what I do. Is that... is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often find yourself having trouble staying focused, sitting still, or thinking before acting in situations outside of work, like at home or during conversations with friends?

Um, outside of work? Well, I mean, I guess I'm pretty much the same everywhere. I definitely like to stay active! At home, I'm usually, you know, buzzing around doing chores or working on a hobby. I don't really sit on the couch for hours on end, but that's just because I like being productive, right? 

With friends... I mean, I love talking to my friends! Sometimes I might get a little excited and jump into the conversation quickly, but it's just because I'm so interested in what they're saying. I don't think I have trouble focusing on them at all. I'm a really good listener, I promise! I just... I might talk with my hands a lot or shift around in my seat, but everyone knows that's just me being me. 

I don't think it causes any real problems. I'm just a high-energy person, which is a good trait to have, don't you think? I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm bouncing off the walls or anything bad like that.
Do you often find yourself starting tasks but not finishing them, or acting on impulse without thinking things through, even if it leads to problems?

Oh, um, no, I really don't think so. I mean, in my line of work, you absolutely have to finish the project, right? You can't just leave a video half-edited! So I definitely make sure to get things done. I wouldn't say I leave tasks unfinished... that just sounds so irresponsible, and I really pride myself on being reliable for my team. 

And as for acting on impulse... well, I guess I'm maybe a little spontaneous sometimes? Like, I might suggest a fun new camera angle on the fly or try a different cut just to see how it looks. But it definitely doesn't lead to problems. I'm always very careful not to mess anything up or cause trouble for anyone else. I always want to do a good job, you know? 

I really hope I'm not coming across as careless or anything like that. I'm actually very dedicated to my work! Am I explaining that okay?

Looking back on your childhood, did you often have trouble staying focused or felt unusually restless or fidgety, even in situations where you were expected to sit still or pay attention, like in school?

Um, well, looking back... I guess I was a pretty, um, eager kid? I really loved participating! But, I mean, I suppose sometimes back in elementary school, my teachers would actually have to move my desk. But I really think it was just because I was so excited to be part of the class, you know? 

I would kind of... blurt out the answers, or I'd find myself popping out of my seat before I even realized I was doing it. And, well, I guess sometimes I might have bothered my classmates a little bit without meaning to. 

I really wasn't trying to be a troublemaker or anything, I promise! I just had a lot of energy and wanted to be involved in everything. That's pretty normal for little kids, right? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad student... I always really wanted to be good for my teachers. Does that make sense?
Looking back, were you already having trouble staying focused or feeling restless before you turned 12?

Um, yeah, I mean, the things I just mentioned about my desk being moved and blurting out answers... that was definitely in elementary school, so, you know, way before I was 12. 

But I really want to make sure I'm not painting the wrong picture here. I wasn't, like, a terror in the classroom or anything! I was just a really enthusiastic kid who loved school a little too much, maybe? I didn't mean to be restless, it's just hard when you're little and you have so much you want to share with the class. 

I hope that's okay? I just really don't want you to think I was a difficult child. I always tried my absolute best to be a good girl for my teachers and my parents. I'm answering this the right way, aren't I?
